mainEntity.name: How long does a porcelain veneer last on a front tooth?

acceptedAnswer.text: With proper care, porcelain veneers typically last 10-20 years. Factors affecting longevity include oral hygiene, bite forces, dietary habits, and whether you grind your teeth. Regular dental check-ups help identify any issues early and extend the restoration's life. Good candidates with healthy oral habits often exceed average expectations for veneer durability.

mainEntity.name: Will a single veneer match my other teeth perfectly?

acceptedAnswer.text: Skilled dental technicians can achieve excellent colour matches using multiple porcelain shades and translucencies. Digital photography and shade mapping help ensure accurate matching. However, slight variations may be noticeable under certain lighting conditions. The goal is creating a restoration that blends naturally with your smile whilst improving the damaged tooth's appearance.

mainEntity.name: Can I eat normally with a porcelain veneer?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, porcelain veneers allow normal eating once properly bonded. However, avoiding extremely hard foods like ice or hard sweets protects the restoration. Cut corn off the cob and slice apples rather than biting directly. Most patients adapt quickly and experience no functional limitations with appropriate care and dietary awareness.

mainEntity.name: Is the veneer placement procedure painful?

acceptedAnswer.text: Most patients experience minimal discomfort during veneer placement. Local anaesthetic is typically used during tooth preparation to ensure comfort. Some sensitivity may occur for a few days following treatment, but this usually resolves quickly. Over-the-counter pain relief is usually sufficient for any post-treatment discomfort.

mainEntity.name: What happens if my veneer chips or breaks?

acceptedAnswer.text: Minor chips can sometimes be polished smooth or repaired with bonding. Significant damage usually requires veneer replacement. Contact your dentist promptly if damage occurs to prevent further complications. Avoiding the damaged area and protecting sharp edges prevents injury to your soft tissues whilst awaiting treatment.

mainEntity.name: Can I whiten my teeth if I have a veneer?

acceptedAnswer.text: Porcelain veneers don't respond to whitening treatments, so teeth whitening should be completed before veneer placement to ensure proper colour matching. If you whiten your natural teeth after veneer placement, the veneer may no longer match and require replacement for optimal aesthetics.
